ChartOptions.description: Common layout, theme, header and interaction options used by chart composites. Width and height describe scene geometry; they do not resize the canvas.

ChartOptions.width.description: Width of the chart's plotting layout in local scene units. Defaults to 30; the optional card adds another 3.2 units across its width.

ChartOptions.height.description: Height of the chart's plotting layout in local scene units. Defaults to 18; the optional card adds another 4.2 units across its height.

ChartOptions.theme.description: Colors, font sizes and stroke sizes for the composite. Defaults to DarkModernTheme. The chart retains this object rather than copying it; existing geometry is not automatically rebuilt when you edit the theme.

ChartOptions.title.description: Optional header text. A truthy title creates an SDFText above the plotting layout and enables the accompanying subtitle.

ChartOptions.subtitle.description: Optional secondary header. It is created only when title is also truthy; a subtitle alone does not create a header.

ChartOptions.showCard.description: Create the background card unless explicitly false. The card is a Rect child placed behind the chart; this option is read during construction.

ChartOptions.showTooltip.description: Create the shared Tooltip unless explicitly false. Individual marks provide the pointer handlers that show it.

ChartOptions.showGrid.description: Let chart implementations create grid lines and tick labels unless explicitly false. It does not disable all axes or category labels.

Chart.constructor.description: Create the shared chart group, optional card, header and tooltip. A concrete subclass then builds its data marks.

parameters.options: The subclass's chart options. Stored by reference; changing this object later does not automatically rebuild marks, scales or headers.

notes: The chart and its marks form an Entity hierarchy. Move, scale or remove the chart as a composite instead of separately moving every bar or label.

Chart.options.description: The original options object supplied to the constructor. This is configuration retained by reference, not a reactive store.

Chart.theme.description: The selected theme object used while constructing marks, labels and overlays. Existing child styles retain their previously assigned values.

Chart.chartWidth.description: Plot layout width in local scene units, initially options.width or 30. Mutating it alone does not rebuild the chart.

Chart.chartHeight.description: Plot layout height in local scene units, initially options.height or 18. Concrete charts subtract their own internal margins from this extent.

Chart.titleEntity.description: The generated title SDFText, if a title was supplied. Use setText for a direct text update; changing options.title alone leaves this entity unchanged.

Chart.subtitleEntity.description: The generated secondary header SDFText, present only when both the title and subtitle were supplied.

Chart.cardBg.description: The optional Rect background owned as a chart child. Its size includes the card padding and its z_index is -0.1.

Chart.tooltip.description: The optional shared Tooltip child. Marks call show and hide from their pointer handlers; the tooltip is part of the chart's hierarchy.

BarDataPoint.description: One categorical bar datum. Its category selects a band, value maps through the chart's numeric scale, and color optionally overrides the palette.

BarDataPoint.category.description: Category label and band lookup key. Use unique keys: BandScale.indexOf resolves a duplicate category to its first band.

BarDataPoint.value.description: Numeric data value, distinct from the bar's world height. The current builder clamps the resulting height to at least 0.01, so it does not draw a separate downward bar for negative values.

BarDataPoint.color.description: Optional per-datum Color. Takes precedence over BarChartOptions.barColor and the cyclic theme palette.

BarChartOptions.description: Categorical data and presentation settings for BarChart. The constructor builds bars once; animateData updates the existing bar slots.

BarChartOptions.data.description: Initial category/value records in display order. An empty array creates no bars, grid ticks or category labels. Prefer finite numeric values and unique categories.

BarChartOptions.barColor.description: Shared fallback bar color. A datum's own color wins; without either override, bars cycle through theme.colors.

BarChartOptions.cornerRadius.description: Bar corner radius in local scene units. Defaults to the smaller of 22% of the band width and 0.4.

BarChartOptions.showLabels.description: Show category labels below the baseline unless explicitly false. This is independent of the numeric value badges and grid tick labels.

BarChartOptions.showValues.description: Create value badges above bars when true. Defaults to off; initial noninteger values use one decimal place, while animateData uses the supplied value string.

BarChartOptions.valuePrefix.description: Text inserted before values in grid ticks, badges and tooltip values. Defaults to an empty string; it does not transform the numeric data.

BarChartOptions.valueSuffix.description: Text inserted after values in grid ticks, badges and tooltip values, such as a unit label. Defaults to an empty string.

BarChartOptions.yRange.description: Explicit [minimum, maximum] numeric data domain. By default the domain is [0, max(largest value, 1) × 1.18]. It maps to a positive-height plotting range, rather than establishing a signed zero axis.

BarChart.bars.description: Generated Rect children in initial data order. animateData addresses these by index; the array is not a reactive data input.

BarChart.labels.description: Generated category-label SDFText children, empty when showLabels is false. animateData does not replace their text.

BarChart.valueLabels.description: Generated numeric badges when showValues is true. Entrance and data animations move these along with their corresponding bars.

BarChart.gridLines.description: Child group containing horizontal grid lines and numeric tick labels. It is still constructed when showGrid is false, but remains empty.

BarChart.axisLine.description: Baseline Line3D spanning the chart's nominal width. It is created separately from the grid and remains when showGrid is false.

BarChart.build.description: Create band and numeric scales, then append grid lines, bars, labels and pointer handlers for the current options.data.
BarChart.build.returnsDescription: No value. An absent or empty dataset returns immediately.
notes: This implementation appends to existing children and tracking arrays; it does not clear a previous build. Construct a replacement chart when categories or layout change, and use animateData for compatible value updates.
The numeric scale created here is retained during animateData. Values outside its domain extrapolate beyond the plotting range rather than automatically expanding the axis.

LineDataPoint.description: One numeric x/y sample for a line series. Samples are connected in array order, not automatically sorted by x.

LineDataPoint.x.description: Horizontal data coordinate, mapped to the chart's local x coordinate through xScale.

LineDataPoint.y.description: Vertical data coordinate, mapped through yScale. This is independent of the camera's world coordinates.

LineDataPoint.label.description: Optional tooltip heading for this sample. Falls back to the series name, then Point. It does not add a permanent text label beside the dot.

LineSeries.description: One ordered sequence of points plus its line/dot styling. Separate series share the chart's x and y scales.

LineSeries.name.description: Optional heading used in a sample's tooltip when that sample has no label. The current builder does not automatically create a legend.

LineSeries.data.description: Samples connected in the supplied order. Sort them yourself when the intended line should advance monotonically along x.

LineSeries.color.description: Color of the line and its dots. Defaults to this series' entry in the cyclic theme palette.

LineSeries.strokeWidth.description: Line width in scene units. Defaults to theme.strokeWidth × 1.8; dot radius is derived from this width.

LineSeries.showDots.description: Set false to suppress this series' dots. Dots are also suppressed when the chart-level showDots is false; a series-level true does not override that global false.

LineChartOptions.description: Series, numeric domains, dots and axis label formatting for LineChart and its AreaChart subclass.

LineChartOptions.series.description: Series sharing a common plot. An empty list produces no scales or marks; each populated series contributes to the inferred domains.

LineChartOptions.xRange.description: Explicit [minimum, maximum] x data domain. Otherwise uses the smallest and largest x values across all series. Equal endpoints collapse mapping to the range start through LinearScale.

LineChartOptions.yRange.description: Explicit [minimum, maximum] y data domain. Otherwise the lower endpoint is min(0, smallest y) and the upper endpoint is largest y × 1.18. Specify a range for all-negative data or consistent comparisons.

LineChartOptions.showDots.description: Create sample dots unless explicitly false, also respecting each series' showDots setting. Tooltip handlers are attached to these dots, not to arbitrary positions along the line.

LineChartOptions.xLabelFormatter.description: Synchronous callback converting an x-axis tick's numeric data value to a string. Only formats the label; it does not change scale mapping.

LineChartOptions.yLabelFormatter.description: Synchronous callback formatting numeric y ticks. Read during build; changing the callback afterward does not regenerate existing labels.

LineChart.constructor.description: Create grid, axis and dot groups, then build the supplied series.

parameters.options: LineChartOptions containing the initial series and shared domains.

LineChart.build.description: Infer or apply shared domains, append grid/tick labels and axes, then connect each series with a Poly and optional sample dots.
LineChart.build.returnsDescription: No value; an absent or empty series list returns without creating scales.
notes: Poly joins the supplied samples as straight segments; this method does not smooth or sort them. Finite data and usable chart dimensions are caller responsibilities.
Calling build again appends new child geometry and tracking arrays without clearing the first build. Recreate the composite for a different series layout.

LineChart.animateIn.description: Prepare the lines at their baseline immediately and return an animation that raises successive samples toward their original y positions.

parameters.options: Uses duration in milliseconds, defaulting to 1800. The implementation supplies its own linear outer rate and per-sample easeOutCubic curve.

LineChart.animateIn.returnsDescription: An Animation to pass to Scene.play; constructing it already resets line/dot positions and visibility.
notes: The point count remains fixed during the animation, while new Vec2 values are produced for each frame.

The current dot update uses the point index against the combined allDots array for every series. Later series can therefore update the first series' dots instead of their own. Disable dots for multi-series entrance animations when that behavior would be misleading.

LineChart.polylines.description: The Poly child for each built series, in series order. Their vertices are mapped chart-local positions, not the original data values.

LineChart.dotsGroup.description: Group of all generated sample Dot children and their tooltip handlers. Dot creation depends on global and per-series showDots settings.

LineChart.gridLines.description: Group of horizontal/vertical grid lines and numeric tick labels. showGrid false leaves this group empty.

LineChart.axisGroup.description: Group containing the separately generated main x-axis line. This is independent of the optional grid group.

LineChart.xScale.description: The LinearScale mapping shared x data values to the local plot range. Created by build when the series list is nonempty; changing it alone does not move existing marks.

LineChart.yScale.description: The shared numeric-to-local-y LinearScale. Existing vertices and dots retain their built positions until explicitly changed.

AreaChartOptions.description: LineChartOptions extended with opacity for the filled area behind each eligible series.

AreaChartOptions.fillOpacity.description: Alpha applied to each series' area color, defaulting to 0.28. The filled polygon closes to the plot's lower baseline, which need not be the y = 0 data coordinate.

AreaChart.areaPolys.description: Filled Poly children behind line strokes. A series with fewer than two points creates no area; areaPolys therefore need not have the same length or indices as the original series list.

AreaChart.constructor.description: Build the inherited line chart, then add a closed area polygon for each series containing at least two samples.

AreaChart.animateIn.description: Return an entrance animation that raises line samples and rebuilds the area boundary at a fixed vertex count.

parameters.options: Uses duration in milliseconds, defaulting to 1800. The implementation supplies its own linear outer rate and eased sample progress.

AreaChart.animateIn.returnsDescription: An Animation for Scene.play. Construction immediately hides the lines, fills and dots and flattens the line vertices.
notes: The animated displacement is clamped to at least 0.005 above the plot baseline. Choose a domain that keeps the intended data above that baseline.

The current implementation assumes areaPolys[s] belongs to polylines[s], although a short series can be skipped while building areas. Use at least two samples per series for the entrance animation. It also inherits the combined-dot indexing limitation described on LineChart.animateIn.

LinearScale.constructor.description: Copy a numeric domain and spatial range into an independent scale.

parameters.range: Output [start, end] coordinates, defaulting to [0, 10]. These are caller-selected units, not necessarily pixels.

LinearScale.domain.description: Mutable numeric input endpoints, copied from the constructor argument. Reversed endpoints are allowed for mapping; ticks only generates an ascending domain.

LinearScale.range.description: Mutable output endpoints in the caller's chosen units. The scale itself does not know the canvas resolution or camera transform.

LinearScale.scale.description: Map one input value by linear interpolation between the domain and range endpoints.

parameters.value: Numeric data value; values outside the domain extrapolate without clamping.

LinearScale.scale.returnsDescription: Mapped output coordinate. Equal domain endpoints return range[0].

LinearScale.invert.description: Apply the reverse linear mapping from the output range to the data domain.

parameters.pixel: An output coordinate in the scale's range units. Despite the parameter name, chart ranges usually use scene units.

LinearScale.invert.returnsDescription: Data value. Equal range endpoints return domain[0]; out-of-range coordinates extrapolate.

LinearScale.ticks.description: Choose a rounded step using 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten and return ascending tick values within the domain.

parameters.count: Positive target tick density, defaulting to 5. It is not an exact returned array length.

LinearScale.ticks.returnsDescription: Numeric ticks rounded to six decimal places. A zero-width or descending domain returns only its first endpoint.
notes: The implementation does not validate count. Supply a finite positive value rather than relying on zero or negative inputs.

BandScale.constructor.description: Copy categorical keys and output endpoints, then clamp both padding fractions into [0, 1].

parameters.domain: Ordered category keys; defaults to an empty array.
parameters.range: Spatial output endpoints, defaulting to [0, 10]. Reversed endpoints reverse placement.
parameters.paddingInner: Fraction of each step left between bands, defaulting to 0.25.
parameters.paddingOuter: Padding at either outer end, measured as a fraction of a step; defaults to 0.15.

BandScale.domain.description: Mutable category list copied from the constructor. Keys are located with indexOf, so duplicate keys use the first matching band.

BandScale.range.description: Mutable output endpoints in caller-selected spatial units. Placement follows their order, while step and bandwidth are nonnegative.

BandScale.paddingInner.description: Fraction of a band step removed from the band's width. Clamped only during construction; direct property writes bypass that clamp.

BandScale.paddingOuter.description: Padding at each range end in step units. Clamped only during construction; direct changes should remain within [0, 1].

BandScale.step.description: Calculate the distance between category band starts from range length, category count and padding.
BandScale.step.returnsDescription: Nonnegative spacing in range units. An empty domain or nonpositive denominator returns 0.

BandScale.bandwidth.description: Calculate the band width as step × (1 − paddingInner).
BandScale.bandwidth.returnsDescription: Width in range units. The sign of a reversed range is applied by placement, not by this width.

BandScale.scale.description: Find the start of a category's band, including outer padding and range direction.

parameters.key: Category key to find using the first matching domain entry.

BandScale.scale.returnsDescription: Band start in range units. An unknown key returns range[0], rather than throwing or producing a missing value.

BandScale.center.description: Return the category's band start plus half its width in the range direction.

parameters.key: Category key. Validate it first if unknown categories should be rejected.

BandScale.center.returnsDescription: Band center. An unknown key still receives the half-band offset from range[0].
